advances: Posterior probabilities on actual unchanged fibers. No transfer of the selected centroid's depth to the prior.

proof:
Brunn–Minkowski and the weighted arithmetic–geometric mean give $V_w^{1/d}\ge\sum_j\lambda_jV_{z_j}^{1/d}\ge\prod_jV_{z_j}^{\lambda_j/d}$. In the ratio the affine term and normalizer cancel and $\sum_j\lambda_j|z_j|^2-|w|^2=\sum_j\lambda_j|z_j-w|^2$. The midpoint case follows by squaring, using $|z-z'|^2\ge4$ on distinct points of the same integer parity and $p_w\le1$. In each parity the product of an unselected weight and the selected maximum is at least the square of the former. There are $|P|-k$ unselected weights, each at most $e^{-t/2}$. The heaviest weight is at least the positive part of the retained bound divided by $k$. The full-volume metronoid in 6769574fc1bd9f8d is the centroid; every ambient containing halfspace thus captures at least a $\Gamma_d$ fraction of that fiber, with a pure-base containing halfspace capturing it all.

Writing the exponent as $-t|z-c|^2/2+t|c|^2/2+(a_t-tc)\cdot z$ gives exponentially vanishing ratios of every nonnearest base against any nearest base, since the remainder is $o(t)$ and $P$ is finite. For exact linear drift and fixed intercept the remaining ratios are constant. Two distinct same-parity nearest bases would have a sampled midpoint with strictly smaller squared distance, by the midpoint identity for the squared norm. Finally $A_t/t=Z_0+B_t/t\to Z_0$ almost surely by the Brownian strong law in the stated observation model. There is a unique nearest base to $Z_0$, namely itself.
statement:
Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite nonempty, with positive compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$, $d\ge1$, satisfying $\sum_j\lambda_jK_{z_j}\subseteq K_w$ whenever $w=\sum_j\lambda_jz_j\in P$ with convex weights. Put $V_z=|K_z|$ and $p_z\propto V_z\exp(a\cdot z-t|z|^2/2)$ for $t\ge0$. Each such anchored relation satisfies
$$
\frac{p_w}{\prod_jp_{z_j}^{\lambda_j}}
=\frac{V_w}{\prod_j V_{z_j}^{\lambda_j}}
 \exp\!\left(\frac t2\sum_j\lambda_j|z_j-w|^2\right)
\ge\exp\!\left(\frac t2\sum_j\lambda_j|z_j-w|^2\right).
$$
For distinct same-parity $z,z'$ with midpoint $w$, one has $p_w^2/(p_zp_{z'})\ge e^{t|z-z'|^2/4}$, hence $p_zp_{z'}\le e^{-t}$. If $k$ parities are occupied, one largest posterior weight per parity retains mass at least $1-(|P|-k)e^{-t/2}$ uniformly in $a$. A largest fiber's centroid therefore has posterior depth at least $(\Gamma_d/k)[1-(|P|-k)e^{-t/2}]_+$, where $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$.

If $a_t/t\to c$, the posterior mass outside the nearest bases to $c$ tends to zero. These bases have distinct parities. If $a_t=tc+b$ with fixed $b$, their limiting weights are proportional to $V_z e^{b\cdot z}$. In the observation process with prior proportional to $V_z$, the posterior tends almost surely to the single hidden base.
title: Finite-time parity concentration for Gaussian tilted mixed volume
